macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street futures rebound as oil retreats and Iran tensions ease slightly
items.summary: U.S. stock index futures edged higher after global markets and oil prices steadied following fresh U.S. strikes on Iran, with investors balancing geopolitical risk against signs of oil easing back. Reuters said the move reflected a rebound in risk appetite after the earlier shock to sentiment.

items.title: Asian and European shares recover as tech stabilizes, but Middle East risks remain
items.summary: Reuters reported that Asian shares climbed and European shares rose in choppy trading, helped by a rebound in technology stocks. Gains were limited by renewed concern over the Middle East conflict and its potential impact on inflation and bonds.

items.title: Oil prices jump on renewed U.S.-Iran conflict fears, reviving inflation concerns
items.summary: Reuters said oil prices rose after fresh U.S. strikes against Iran, with market attention focused on the risk to the Strait of Hormuz and broader supply disruptions. The move added pressure on inflation-sensitive assets and bond markets.

items.title: Semiconductor stocks wobble after Iran tensions and weak Samsung signals
items.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. semiconductor stocks were under pressure after renewed U.S.-Iran tensions and disappointing signals from Samsung Electronics rattled confidence in the AI trade. Micron Technology also announced plans to invest more than $250 billion in the U.S. through 2035.

items.title: Global equity pressure remains uneven, with U.S. futures and tech leading sentiment
items.summary: MarketScreener noted that S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures were ticking up as tech shares stabilized, but its 24-hour most-mentioned list still showed weakness in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100. The same feed highlighted sharp moves in names such as Rheinmetall, Hyundai Motor, Carnival, and Accenture.

items.title: Fed officials still flagged inflation risks, while New Zealand raised rates
items.summary: The Financial Times reported that some Fed officials saw the need for future rate rises to contain inflation, indicating that policy makers remain worried about price pressures. The FT also said the Reserve Bank of New Zealand raised rates for the first time in three years and signaled more tightening could follow.

items.title: India faces higher inflation and weaker currency amid energy shock concerns
items.summary: Reuters and Moneycontrol reported that India’s inflation likely moved above the RBI’s 4% target in June, while the rupee fell to 95.55 per U.S. dollar. Separate reports said the ADB cut India’s FY27 growth forecast to 6.6%, citing higher energy prices, and the IMF trimmed its FY27 growth estimate to 6.4%.

items.title: China price data points to rising factory-gate pressure
items.summary: Reuters said China’s producer inflation rose to a near four-year high, with cost pressures still elevated for domestic manufacturers. The move was reinforced by Investing.com’s calendar data showing China’s June PPI at 4.1% year over year.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades above $63K as risk appetite improves
items.summary: Bitcoin climbed above $63,000, with multiple outlets linking the move to easing oil prices and broader risk-on sentiment. Cointelegraph also reported BTC around $64,000 after whales and a stronger Coinbase premium supported the market.

items.title: Bitcoin price momentum points to fresh multi-week highs
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported Bitcoin returning to about $64.3K and said new three-week highs may be imminent, while market coverage noted renewed demand from large holders. This was one of the day’s clearest major price-movement stories.

items.title: CLARITY Act debate intensifies as Congress moves toward a key vote
items.summary: Crypto.news reported that Paul Grewal exited Coinbase’s legal leadership ahead of a crucial CLARITY vote, and separately said the Trump White House rejected SEC snub claims before the showdown. The reporting highlights fast-moving U.S. crypto regulation developments.

items.title: Hong Kong tightens crypto platform security rules
items.summary: crypto.news reported that Hong Kong’s SFC is forcing crypto platforms to abandon SMS authentication, reflecting a continued regulatory push on exchange and custody security. This is one of the clearest new compliance actions in the past 24 hours.

items.title: MiCA scrutiny expands to crypto custodians in Europe
items.summary: Cointelegraph reported that MiCA licensing is only the beginning and that crypto custodians now face additional scrutiny in Europe. The story suggests regulators are widening oversight beyond basic licensing.

items.title: Bitdeer announces $36 million Nevada factory to expand Bitcoin mining
items.summary: crypto.news reported that Bitdeer unveiled a new Nevada factory investment as it looks to strengthen its Bitcoin mining operations. The move stands out as a notable project and infrastructure development.

items.title: XRP gains on renewed Ripple-linked payments narrative
items.summary: crypto.news reported XRP rising as SWIFT taps Ripple-linked banks for blockchain payments. The development is notable because it reinforces the token’s role in ongoing institutional payments discussions.

items.title: PayPal expands PYUSD to Polygon
items.summary: crypto.news reported that PayPal is bringing its PYUSD stablecoin to Polygon’s Open Money Stack. This adds another significant mainstream payments and stablecoin integration story from the day.

items.title: INTERPOL operation disrupts illicit crypto transfers
items.summary: crypto.news reported that an INTERPOL operation blocked illicit crypto transfers and led to 5,811 arrests. The action is a major law-enforcement development with direct relevance to the crypto sector.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation details AI limits in bug detection
items.summary: crypto.news reported that the Ethereum Foundation explained why AI still fails to find real bugs reliably. While not a market-moving headline, it is a notable project-development update for Ethereum’s technical ecosystem.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent inside ChatGPT designed to execute tasks across applications and files, expanding its push into enterprise automation. Reuters says the release intensifies competition in professional AI tools.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The release adds a new multimodal capability aimed at more natural conversational AI.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to Muse Spark 1.1 in a public API preview, positioning the model as a stronger option for advanced coding and business use. Reuters reports the move as a direct challenge to Anthropic and OpenAI's paid model offerings.

items.title: xAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: xAI launched Grok 4.5, describing it as its most intelligent model yet and targeting coding and agentic tasks. The release highlights the accelerating race among frontier model developers.

items.title: Anthropic adds Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body meant to keep the company aligned with its public mission. The move underscores growing emphasis on AI governance and mission oversight.

items.title: Meta plans major Alberta data center for AI capacity
items.summary: Meta announced it will build a large data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada, to expand compute capacity for AI. The investment reflects a broader industry trend toward rapid infrastructure buildout.

items.title: OpenAI copyright dispute escalates with sanctions request
items.summary: The New York Times-led group asked a federal court to sanction OpenAI, alleging it misled the court about its ability to search systems for evidence related to copyrighted articles used in training. The case adds to ongoing legal pressure over AI training data.

items.title: Italy fines Character.AI owner over data protection breaches
items.summary: Italy's data protection authority fined Character Technologies, the owner of Character.AI, €158,000 for alleged breaches of data protection rules. The decision adds to regulatory scrutiny of consumer AI products in Europe.

items.title: Ollama raises $65 million to support local AI model deployment
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that Ollama, a tool for running open-weight AI models locally, raised a $65 million Series B. The funding signals continued investor interest in developer tools for open-model deployment.

items.title: Gradium raises $100 million seed round for AI voice tech
items.summary: TechCrunch reported that Paris-based AI voice startup Gradium raised a $100 million seed round backed by Nvidia. The deal reflects strong capital flows into speech and voice AI startups.
